stories.title: Google Patches Pixel Modem Flaw Amid Signs of Limited Targeted Exploitation
stories.abstract: CISA has updated its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog to include six flaws affecting the Linux kernel, Google Pixel devices, Cisco Identity Services Engine, and Acronis Backup. These additions confirm active exploitation of these vulnerabilities in the wild.
stories.why: These vulnerabilities are actively being used by threat actors, increasing the risk of unauthorized access or system compromise for organizations using these products.
stories.action: Review your environment for these products and apply the latest security patches immediately.

stories.title: ABB Ability Edgenius
stories.abstract: ABB has released a security update for Ability Edgenius versions 3.2.0.0 through 3.2.4.0 to address a Linux kernel vulnerability known as Copy Fail. This flaw allows authenticated local users or compromised containers to escalate privileges to root, granting full system control.
stories.why: Privilege escalation in industrial control software poses a critical risk to operational technology environments and infrastructure integrity.
stories.action: Update ABB Ability Edgenius to version 3.2.4.1 or later.

stories.title: Cisco Warns of New Zero-Day ISE Auth Bypass (CVSS 10.0) Exploited in Active Attacks
stories.abstract: Cisco has disclosed three vulnerabilities affecting Identity Services Engine and ISE Passive Identity Connector. The most critical flaw, CVE-2026-76460, allows unauthenticated remote attackers to bypass authentication via an API endpoint and is currently being exploited in the wild.
stories.why: The critical flaw permits full administrative access and system compromise, making it a high-priority target for threat actors.
stories.action: Apply the latest security patches provided by Cisco immediately.

stories.title: Cisco security advisory (AV26-932)
stories.abstract: Cisco has disclosed multiple critical vulnerabilities across its Secure Firewall, Management Center, Identity Services Engine, Nexus Dashboard, and Adaptive Security Appliance product lines. Additionally, CVE-2026-76461 in Secure Email Gateway is confirmed to be under active exploitation.
stories.why: Active exploitation of CVE-2026-76461 and the broad scope of these patches present a significant risk to enterprise network perimeters and identity infrastructure.
stories.action: Update Cisco Secure Email Gateway and all listed firewall and identity software to the specified versions.

stories.title: Gyazo Breach Exposes 23.62 Million User Records and 490 Million Image Metadata Records
stories.abstract: Image-sharing platform Gyazo suffered a significant data breach after attackers exploited a server-side vulnerability. The incident exposed approximately 23.6 million user records, including email addresses and password hashes, alongside nearly 500 million image metadata entries.
stories.why: The exposure of password hashes and email addresses creates a high risk of credential stuffing and targeted phishing campaigns against affected users.
stories.action: Reset passwords and enable multi-factor authentication if you have a Gyazo account.

stories.title: Android security advisory – September 2026 monthly rollup (AV26-920) – Update 1
stories.abstract: Google has released its September 2026 security updates for Android. Notably, the vulnerability tracked as CVE-2026-58704 is currently being actively exploited in the wild and has been added to CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.
stories.why: Active exploitation of Android vulnerabilities poses a direct risk of device compromise and unauthorized access to sensitive user data.
stories.action: Apply the September 2026 Android security patches immediately.

stories.title: Microsoft Patches CVSS 10.0 Azure AI Foundry Flaw Enabling Unauthorized Privilege Escalation
China-Aligned FamousSparrow Deploys SparroWocky Backdoor Across Latin America
stories.abstract: The state-sponsored threat group FamousSparrow is utilizing a newly identified modular C++ backdoor, dubbed SparroWocky, to compromise government entities throughout Latin America. The campaign, active since August 2025, appears linked to broader geopolitical competition for regional influence.
stories.why: This highlights the continued evolution of Chinese-aligned espionage toolsets targeting government infrastructure to facilitate long-term intelligence gathering.

stories.title: Meta’s Copyright System Is Being Weaponized Against Albanian Protesters
stories.abstract: Albanian activists participating in the Flamingo Revolution are facing mass account suspensions on Instagram. These disruptions appear to stem from the weaponization of Meta’s automated copyright enforcement tools, which are being exploited to silence political dissent and suppress protest-related content.
stories.why: Automated content moderation systems are vulnerable to coordinated abuse, allowing malicious actors to censor political speech through false copyright claims.

stories.title: Brevo supply-chain attack injected ClickFix scripts on customer sites
stories.abstract: Attackers compromised a Brevo API key to deploy a malicious Cloudflare worker. This allowed the injection of harmful ClickFix scripts into approximately 100,000 customer websites, facilitating the distribution of malware to end users.
stories.why: Supply chain compromises via API keys demonstrate the critical need for strict credential rotation and monitoring of third-party infrastructure integrations.
stories.action: Review Cloudflare worker configurations and audit third-party API key access logs for unauthorized modifications.

stories.title: Google security advisory (AV26-939)
stories.abstract: Google has released a security update for Chrome to address multiple vulnerabilities. Users running versions prior to 153.0.8010.53 are at risk and should transition to the latest stable release to ensure browser security.
stories.why: Unpatched browsers are primary vectors for remote code execution and data theft via malicious web content.
stories.action: Update Chrome to version 153.0.8010.53 or later.

stories.title: FBI, Coast Guard boarded hacked oil tankers heading towards US coast
stories.abstract: Federal authorities and the Coast Guard boarded two oil tankers after discovering unauthorized network intrusions. In at least one instance, the attackers successfully disrupted the vessel's navigation and propulsion controls, raising significant concerns regarding the security of maritime industrial control systems.
stories.why: The ability to remotely manipulate critical propulsion and navigation systems on large commercial vessels represents a severe kinetic threat to maritime infrastructure.

stories.title: Critical Check Point Management Flaw Lets Unauthenticated Attackers Run Code as Root
stories.abstract: Check Point has patched a critical vulnerability in its Security Management and Log Servers. The flaw allows unauthenticated remote attackers to execute arbitrary code with root privileges, potentially granting full control over firewall policies and administrative access.
stories.why: Compromise of a central management server provides an attacker with total visibility and control over an organization's entire network security infrastructure.
stories.action: Apply the fix immediately via the Check Point LivePatch update channel.

stories.title: Cisco drops another exploited zero-day, this time a perfect 10
stories.abstract: Cisco has disclosed a critical authentication bypass vulnerability affecting its Identity Services Engine. The flaw is currently being exploited in the wild, marking the second high-severity zero-day incident for the vendor within a single week.
stories.why: Active exploitation of authentication bypasses in identity management infrastructure poses a severe risk of unauthorized network access and privilege escalation.
stories.action: Check Cisco's security advisory and apply the recommended patches or mitigations immediately.

stories.title: U.S. Seizes NightmareStresser Domains Linked to Hundreds of Thousands of DDoS Attacks
stories.abstract: Law enforcement agencies, led by the FBI, have seized the domains for NightmareStresser, a prominent DDoS-for-hire platform that has operated since 2022. The site is now offline, displaying a federal seizure notice to visitors.
stories.why: This disruption removes a significant tool used by cybercriminals to launch disruptive attacks against organizations and infrastructure.

stories.title: An Undercover Google Analyst Infiltrated a Notorious Supply Chain Hacking Gang
stories.abstract: Google threat researchers successfully embedded an analyst within TeamPCP, the hacking collective responsible for a massive, widespread software supply chain compromise. This deep-cover operation provided unique visibility into the group's tactics and internal operations during their extensive campaign against thousands of organizations.
stories.why: It demonstrates the effectiveness of human intelligence in tracking sophisticated supply chain threats that evade traditional automated detection methods.

stories.title: Critical Orkes Conductor Vulnerability Exploited in Attacks
stories.abstract: Attackers are actively exploiting an unauthenticated remote code execution flaw in Orkes Conductor. By injecting malicious code through inline workflow definitions, unauthorized actors can gain control over affected systems.
stories.why: Unauthenticated RCE vulnerabilities in workflow orchestration engines present a high risk of full environment compromise and lateral movement.
stories.action: Update Orkes Conductor to the latest patched version immediately.

stories.title: In Other News: Ransomware Developer Sentenced, Plugin4Shell AI Attack, Critical SAP Flaw
stories.abstract: Recent security developments include the sentencing of a ransomware developer, the emergence of AI-driven Plugin4Shell exploitation techniques, and the discovery of a critical vulnerability affecting SAP software environments.
stories.why: These incidents highlight evolving attack vectors targeting both enterprise software infrastructure and the increasing integration of AI tools in malicious campaigns.

stories.title: Grafana security advisory (AV26-936)
stories.abstract: Grafana has disclosed a cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability affecting the Geomap panel within multiple versions of its OSS software. The flaw impacts various releases across the 12.x and 13.x branches, potentially allowing attackers to execute malicious scripts via the MapLibre integration.
stories.why: XSS vulnerabilities in monitoring dashboards can lead to session hijacking or unauthorized actions performed by authenticated administrative users.
stories.action: Review the official Grafana security advisory and update to the latest patched version immediately.

stories.title: Transparent Tribe Deploys New Rust Backdoor Using Private GitHub Repositories for C2
stories.abstract: The APT36 group is targeting Indian and Afghan government and defense sectors with a new suite of malware. These tools, including RUSTYSHADE and RUSTYMOVE, utilize private GitHub repositories for command-and-control communication to evade detection during their espionage campaigns.
stories.why: This campaign demonstrates an evolving preference for Rust-based tooling and the abuse of legitimate hosting platforms to bypass traditional network security controls.

stories.title: Researchers used Claude to hack OpenAI
RatHat Android Malware Abuses ADB to Retain Shell Access After Uninstall
stories.abstract: A new Android malware strain dubbed RatHat utilizes AI-driven automation to navigate infected devices. Distributed through malicious SMS and deceptive advertisements, the malware maintains persistent shell access via the Android Debug Bridge, allowing it to remain functional even after the primary application is removed.
stories.why: The use of AI for automated device navigation and persistent ADB-based access significantly complicates incident response and malware removal for mobile security teams.

stories.title: Bransys ELD
stories.abstract: Bransys ELD devices contain multiple vulnerabilities, including hardcoded MQTT credentials and cleartext data transmission. Exploitation allows unauthorized access to sensitive telemetry data and firmware across various transportation carriers.
stories.why: Hardcoded credentials in fleet management hardware expose real-time location and operational data for critical infrastructure transportation systems.
stories.action: Update Bransys ELD to version 11.00.00 or later for Android and 1.1.54 or later for iOS.

stories.title: Cisco Secure Email Gateway Flaw Exploited in the Wild, Enables Root Command Execution
stories.abstract: Cisco confirmed active exploitation of a critical vulnerability in its Secure Email Gateway's AsyncOS software. The flaw, stemming from improper email parsing validation, allows unauthenticated remote attackers to execute arbitrary commands with root-level privileges on affected systems.
stories.why: The vulnerability allows full system compromise via remote code execution, posing a severe risk to perimeter security infrastructure.
stories.action: Apply the latest Cisco security patches immediately.

stories.title: Maximum Severity GitLab Flaw Puts Supply Chains at Risk
stories.abstract: GitLab has patched a critical path traversal vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-85706, which carries a maximum CVSS score of 10.0. CISA has confirmed active exploitation of this flaw, which impacts both Community and Enterprise editions of the platform.
stories.why: The vulnerability allows unauthorized file access, potentially compromising CI/CD pipelines and sensitive supply chain credentials.
stories.action: Update GitLab instances to the latest patched version immediately.

stories.title: Threat Intelligence Alone Won't Close the Exploitation Gap
stories.abstract: Adversaries are increasingly leveraging AI to weaponize vulnerabilities and leaked credentials at speeds that outpace traditional security team response times. This acceleration creates a significant gap between initial exposure and successful exploitation, rendering standard manual triage processes insufficient for modern threat landscapes.
stories.why: Security teams must shift from reactive triage to automated, risk-based prioritization to counter AI-driven exploitation speed.

stories.title: Mitsubishi Electric GX Works3 and Motion Control Settings
stories.abstract: A vulnerability in Mitsubishi Electric's GX Works3 and Motion Control Settings allows local attackers to bypass authentication. By modifying memory during execution, unauthorized users can view, alter, or delete critical control programs, potentially disrupting industrial operations.
stories.why: This flaw enables unauthorized manipulation of industrial control logic, posing a significant risk to the integrity and availability of manufacturing systems.

stories.title: Hackers reveal how Flock cameras really track cars and people
stories.abstract: Security researchers successfully compromised a Flock Safety surveillance camera, gaining access to its internal software. The investigation revealed the device captured over 1.6 million images and possessed the capability to identify individual pedestrians in addition to tracking vehicle license plates.
stories.why: This highlights significant privacy risks and potential surveillance overreach inherent in automated license plate recognition systems deployed by law enforcement.

stories.title: Claimed Bug Bounty Hunter Likely Used LLM to Build PhantomRaven npm Stealer
stories.abstract: A threat actor is distributing a JavaScript-based information stealer called PhantomRaven through the npm registry. Researchers believe the malware was authored using large language models, evidenced by specific coding patterns, excessive comments, and leftover placeholder text found within the malicious packages.
stories.why: The use of LLMs to generate functional malware lowers the barrier to entry for attackers, enabling rapid creation of sophisticated, obfuscated malicious packages.

stories.title: Google says some Pixel phone owners were hacked in zero-day attacks
stories.abstract: Google has confirmed that a vulnerability within the modem firmware of certain Pixel devices is currently being subjected to limited, targeted exploitation by malicious actors.
stories.why: Exploitation of baseband vulnerabilities can allow remote code execution or unauthorized access, bypassing standard OS-level security protections.
stories.action: Check for and install the latest available security updates for your Pixel device immediately.

stories.title: Critical Docker Sandboxes Flaw Lets Malicious Guest Code Read and Modify macOS Host Files
stories.abstract: A critical vulnerability in Docker Sandboxes for macOS allows guest virtual machines to bypass directory restrictions. An attacker can exploit this flaw to read or modify arbitrary files on the host system, operating with the privileges of the user running the Docker process.
stories.why: This represents a full container escape, granting unauthorized access to the host filesystem and potentially leading to complete system compromise.
stories.action: Update Docker Sandboxes to the latest patched version immediately.

stories.title: New Settra Ransomware Variant Deployed in Attacks on Retail and Manufacturing
stories.abstract: Security researchers identified a new ransomware strain dubbed Settra. The malware has been observed in recent campaigns targeting the retail and manufacturing sectors, where attackers utilized specific post-compromise tactics to facilitate their operations.
stories.why: Understanding the TTPs of emerging ransomware variants is critical for developing effective detection and response strategies against evolving extortion threats.

stories.title: Critical Unbound DNSSEC Validator Flaw Could Allow RCE via a Malicious DNS Zone
stories.abstract: NLnet Labs released Unbound version 1.26.1 to address a critical heap overflow vulnerability within its DNSSEC validator. An attacker managing a malicious DNS zone could exploit this flaw to execute arbitrary code on systems running older versions of the resolver.
stories.why: Remote code execution in a core DNS component poses a severe risk to network infrastructure and service availability.
stories.action: Update Unbound to version 1.26.1 immediately.

stories.title: Mitsubishi Electric CC-Link IE TSN Communication Protocol (Update A)
Hitachi Energy FACTS Control Platform (FCP)
stories.abstract: Hitachi Energy identified vulnerabilities in its FACTS Control Platform (FCP) specifically affecting systems equipped with the GWS component deployed since 2020. Exploitation could compromise the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of critical power infrastructure components like SVC Light and Static Var Compensators.
stories.why: These vulnerabilities impact industrial control systems managing high-voltage power grids, posing significant risks to operational technology stability and infrastructure security.
stories.action: Review Hitachi Energy's advisory and apply recommended mitigations for GWS-equipped FACTS Control Platform deployments.

stories.title: Tanium security advisory (AV26-935)
stories.abstract: Tanium has disclosed a security vulnerability affecting its Threat Response module. The flaw impacts specific versions of the software, necessitating updates to versions 4.12.317, 4.17.289, 4.9.447, or newer to mitigate potential risks.
stories.why: Unpatched security management tools can be leveraged by attackers to gain elevated control over enterprise endpoints.
stories.action: Update Tanium Threat Response to the specified patched versions immediately.

stories.title: Schneider Electric NetBotz 5 750/755
stories.abstract: Schneider Electric has disclosed two vulnerabilities, including OS command injection and SQL injection, affecting NetBotz 5 750 and 755 environmental monitoring units running firmware version 5.5.2 or earlier. Exploitation could allow unauthorized remote code execution and data access.
stories.why: These devices monitor critical physical infrastructure; compromise allows attackers to manipulate environmental controls or gain unauthorized access to sensitive facility data.
stories.action: Update NetBotz 5 750 and 755 firmware to a version beyond 5.5.2.

stories.title: Dell security advisory (AV26-934)
stories.abstract: Dell has released security updates addressing multiple vulnerabilities across several product lines, including Networking OS10, OpenManage Server Administrator, ObjectScale, Elastic Cloud Storage, the Update Package Framework, Wyse Management Suite, and Repository Manager.
stories.why: These vulnerabilities affect critical infrastructure and management software, potentially allowing unauthorized access or system compromise if left unpatched.
stories.action: Review the specific Dell Security Advisories and apply the latest firmware and software updates.

stories.title: Schneider Electric PowerChute Serial Shutdown
stories.abstract: Schneider Electric has disclosed an authentication vulnerability in PowerChute Serial Shutdown versions 1.6 and earlier. The flaw involves improper restriction of excessive authentication attempts, which could allow unauthorized access or operational disruption within the UPS management software.
stories.why: Exploitation could lead to unauthorized system access or service outages in critical infrastructure environments relying on this power management software.
stories.action: Update PowerChute Serial Shutdown to the latest version provided by Schneider Electric.

stories.title: HTTP QUERY Method: The Grey Zone Between GET And POST., (Fri, Sep 18th)
stories.abstract: The IETF has introduced a new HTTP method called QUERY, standardized under RFC 10008. This verb is designed to handle data retrieval requests that involve complex parameters, effectively bridging the functional gap between standard GET and POST methods.
stories.why: Security teams must evaluate how existing WAFs, proxies, and application logic handle this new verb to prevent bypasses or unexpected request processing.

stories.title: New RatHat Android malware uses AI to automate device control
stories.abstract: Researchers identified RatHat, a novel Android trojan that integrates an AI-driven subsystem. This feature assists remote operators in navigating infected devices, streamlining the process of executing malicious commands and bypassing standard manual interaction hurdles during unauthorized access.
stories.why: The integration of AI into mobile malware suggests a shift toward automated, more efficient remote control and data exfiltration capabilities.

stories.title: Check Point security advisory (AV26-933)
stories.abstract: Check Point has disclosed a stack overflow vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-91843, affecting the login process for several Security Management and Log Server versions. The flaw impacts multiple R81 and R82 releases, potentially allowing unauthorized memory corruption during authentication.
stories.why: Exploitation of authentication-related stack overflows can lead to remote code execution or service disruption on critical management infrastructure.
stories.action: Review Check Point advisory sk1000155 and apply the latest Jumbo Hotfix updates.

stories.title: Fake LastPass Authenticator GitHub repos push new Rapuncel infostealer
stories.abstract: Threat actors are using SEO-poisoned GitHub repositories to distribute a new information-stealing malware dubbed Rapuncel. These repositories masquerade as legitimate software from well-known firms to trick developers into downloading malicious payloads.
stories.why: This campaign demonstrates how attackers leverage trusted platforms and search engine optimization to deliver novel malware directly to technical users.
stories.action: Audit GitHub repository dependencies and verify source authenticity before executing any downloaded code.

stories.title: Microsoft Issues Emergency Fixes After Massive Patch Tuesday
stories.abstract: Microsoft released emergency out-of-band updates to address technical regressions introduced during the recent Patch Tuesday cycle. These fixes resolve stability and functional problems that emerged immediately following the deployment of the initial monthly security batch.
stories.why: Unexpected post-patch instability can disrupt critical infrastructure and force emergency maintenance windows outside of standard operational schedules.
stories.action: Review and deploy the latest out-of-band updates from Microsoft to resolve recent patch regressions.

stories.title: Schneider Electric Modicon M340 Controller and Communication Modules
stories.abstract: Schneider Electric has identified a security vulnerability affecting several Modicon M340 programmable automation controllers and associated Ethernet communication modules. The company is currently evaluating the impact and potential remediation steps for these industrial control system components.
stories.why: Unpatched vulnerabilities in industrial controllers can allow unauthorized access or disruption to critical operational technology environments.
stories.action: Monitor the Schneider Electric security portal for upcoming firmware updates and mitigation guidance.

stories.title: ISC Stormcast For Friday, September 18th, 2026 https://isc.sans.edu/podcastdetail/10100, (Fri, Sep 18th)
stories.abstract: The provided source material for the SANS ISC Stormcast dated September 18, 2026, contains no descriptive content or summary of the day's security events, rendering it impossible to provide a meaningful update on current threats or vulnerabilities.

stories.title: Manufacturing Accounts for 22% of all Ransomware Victims
stories.abstract: Manufacturing has emerged as the primary target for ransomware operators, experiencing a significant surge in successful attacks throughout the first half of 2026. Data indicates this sector now accounts for over one-fifth of all global ransomware incidents.
stories.why: The sector's reliance on legacy operational technology and high uptime requirements makes it a lucrative and vulnerable target for extortion.

stories.title: LausivLoader analysis, or how to pass data between malware stages, (Thu, Sep 17th)
stories.abstract: Security researchers identified a new malware strain dubbed LausivLoader, distributed via phishing emails masquerading as business inquiries. The loader employs sophisticated techniques to pass data between execution stages, complicating detection and analysis for defenders monitoring email gateways.
stories.why: Understanding novel multi-stage loading techniques is critical for improving endpoint detection and response strategies against evolving modular malware.

stories.title: Adversary simulation: what you need to know
stories.abstract: The NCSC has published guidance on adversary simulation, also known as red teaming. This practice involves conducting controlled exercises to evaluate an organization's defensive capabilities, specifically focusing on its capacity to identify, mitigate, and react to simulated cyber threats.
stories.why: Structured red teaming exercises provide empirical data on how effectively security controls and incident response teams perform against realistic attack vectors.

stories.title: UK and allies expose spyware used by Iranian state actors to target dissidents, activists and journalists
stories.abstract: The UK's NCSC and international partners have issued an advisory regarding Chosen Brick, a sophisticated spyware strain linked to Iranian state actors. The malware is primarily engineered to conduct surveillance on political dissidents and targeted individuals.
stories.why: This highlights evolving state-sponsored espionage tactics and provides specific indicators for organizations to identify and mitigate targeted surveillance threats.

stories.title: LG Caught Spying in Your Living Room, Miami Crypto King Gets Life, and the AI Apocalypse Debate
stories.abstract: Researchers discovered that LG smart TVs continue recording and transcribing ambient audio even when the devices are powered off or set to ignore voice commands. These private conversations are stored as plaintext files on the television's local storage, creating significant privacy and surveillance risks.
stories.why: Unauthorized audio collection by consumer IoT devices poses a severe privacy threat and potential vector for sensitive data exposure in home environments.

stories.title: Zero-Day Flaw in TP-Link Cameras Enables Eavesdropping
stories.abstract: Researchers at OPSWAT identified two zero-day vulnerabilities within TP-Link camera firmware. These flaws could potentially allow unauthorized actors to intercept audio or video feeds, compromising the privacy and security of users relying on these devices for surveillance.
stories.why: Compromised IoT devices serve as entry points for network lateral movement and persistent surveillance of sensitive environments.

stories.title: Ransomware incidents in Japan in the first half of 2026: Investigation of The Gentlemen’s infrastructure and evidence of Qilin's AI use
stories.abstract: Ransomware attacks in Japan increased by nearly 5% during the first half of 2026. The Gentlemen emerged as the primary threat actor, while Qilin demonstrated the integration of artificial intelligence into its operations. Small and medium-sized enterprises remain the most frequent targets.
stories.why: The shift toward AI-assisted ransomware and the targeting of smaller, less-resourced organizations highlights evolving adversary tactics and broader attack surfaces.

stories.title: 404 Media x The Intercept Live: How AI Is Used to Surveil and Kill
stories.abstract: Journalists from 404 Media and The Intercept are hosting a discussion regarding the intersection of private sector technology and government surveillance, specifically focusing on the integration of artificial intelligence into modern military operations and lethal targeting systems.
stories.why: It highlights the growing ethical and security risks associated with the privatization of advanced surveillance and autonomous weapon technologies.

stories.title: Attackers Exploit WooCommerce Wholesale Lead Capture Flaw to Plant PHP Web Shells
stories.abstract: Unauthenticated attackers are exploiting a critical vulnerability in the WooCommerce Wholesale Lead Capture plugin for WordPress. The flaw allows remote actors to upload arbitrary files, enabling the deployment of PHP webshells and full remote code execution on affected sites.
stories.why: Remote code execution vulnerabilities in widely used plugins provide attackers with an easy path to full server compromise and persistent backdoor access.
stories.action: Update the WooCommerce Wholesale Lead Capture plugin to the latest available version immediately.

stories.title: Webinar: Which Google Workspace security controls actually matter?
stories.abstract: A webinar is being hosted to evaluate the effectiveness of various Google Workspace security configurations. The session aims to help resource-constrained security teams prioritize high-impact controls by analyzing patterns observed in actual enterprise data breaches.
stories.why: Optimizing security spend and configuration efforts is critical for reducing attack surfaces in cloud-based collaboration environments.

stories.title: Cyber Adversary Simulation (CyAS): scheme documents now available
stories.abstract: The UK's NCSC has published new guidance detailing its framework for cyber adversary simulation. The documentation outlines the agency's expectations for high-quality testing and defines the standards required for providers to deliver assured security assessments.
stories.why: It provides a standardized benchmark for evaluating red teaming and penetration testing services, helping organizations verify the quality of their security assessments.

stories.title: Attackers Exploit Issabel Framework Flaw Enabling Unauthenticated OS Command Execution
stories.abstract: The Issabel PBX framework is currently under active attack due to a critical vulnerability, CVE-2026-89026. This flaw stems from a hard-coded credential issue, allowing remote, unauthenticated actors to execute arbitrary operating system commands on affected systems.
stories.why: Remote code execution vulnerabilities in unified communications infrastructure provide attackers with a direct foothold into internal networks and sensitive voice traffic.
stories.action: Apply the latest security patches for the Issabel Framework immediately.

stories.title: I Built a Portal to the Internet in Minecraft
stories.abstract: The provided source material describes promotional links for cybersecurity training, newsletters, and infrastructure tools. It does not contain information regarding a Minecraft-based internet portal or any specific security incident or vulnerability.

stories.title: Iran-Linked Handala Hack Tied to HEAVYGRAM Telegram Backdoor That Can Steal Passwords
stories.abstract: The Iran-aligned group Handala is utilizing a Telegram-based backdoor dubbed HEAVYGRAM to conduct surveillance. The malware enables remote command execution, session file theft, and system reconnaissance, often paired with a Delphi utility to facilitate data exfiltration and unauthorized access.
stories.why: This campaign demonstrates how threat actors leverage legitimate messaging platforms to bypass security controls and maintain persistent access to compromised endpoints.
